calls.head: Unstoppable force vs. Immovable object
calls.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Panthers take a lot of penalties and the Red Wings draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.head: DeBrincat gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Panthers keep sending Lundell’s line (Luostarinen, Lundell and Devine) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Paul Maurice has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Red Wings’ first line is DeBrincat, Finnie and Arvidsson.

surprises.head: Florida shut down Detroit’s power play
surprises.body: Detroit’s power play created 0.9 expected goals per 60, against their usual 9.0 (about 7.7 against Florida) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Detroit hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Detroit usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 56 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 109 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Forsling sparks the Panthers back from three down
paras: What a comeback. Sam Reinhart struck first for the Panthers early in the first, but J.T. Compher made it 1-1 for Detroit just 15 seconds later. Andreas Englund scored his first goal for Detroit midway through the period to put the Red Wings ahead 2-1. Lucas Raymond pushed the lead to 3-1 just 17 seconds into the period, and Alex DeBrincat and Sam Bennett dropped the gloves early in the second. Marco Kasper made it 4-1 for the Red Wings midway through the period, and that was all they would get. Gustav Forsling cut Detroit’s lead to 4-2 with 18 seconds left in the second, and Anton Lundell pulled the Panthers within one early in the third. Lars Eller tied it up with three and a half minutes left. Lundell scored his second of the night 51 seconds later to put the Panthers ahead for good. Carter Verhaeghe finished with three assists.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Panthers had six shots in the first period and trailed 2-1, then outshot the Red Wings 23-16 the rest of the way. Akira Schmid made 24 saves for the Panthers, and John Gibson allowed five goals on 29 shots. The Panthers improved to 11-7-2, fifth in the Atlantic, while the Wings fell to 7-10-3, still last in the Atlantic.
